answers.confusing_rules: 1) Scout groups: I had to work out for myself that Astral Visits (Oracle/Ritualist guesses) and Katana passing don't link anyone, but Sleepwalker visits do. The Scout text says groups are "as for the Cartographer", so I had to go to a second role's text to find the linking rules. A short line in the Scout text saying what does and doesn't link would help. 2) The Archivist's fakes can repeat a non-unique role. Dave's list showed "Diviner x2" with no Diviner in the game, and the whole town read that as a "real Yakuza Diviner". The rule technically allows it, but it is easy to miss that two copies of a role can both be fakes. 3) Two Drowsy players (Bob and Carol) being blocked on Night 1 with no blocker looked exactly like one or two real blockers. That is legal, but the town can't tell the difference at all.
answers.missing_information: The public ledger doesn't record each player's stated trial and nomination votes. I had to copy them into my notepad by hand to compare them with the totals. It also doesn't record who claimed what about whom on which night (for example "Ivan says he tracked Frank N1"), so cross-checking claimed visits against my visit-group results took a lot of manual reconstruction. On Night 2 I also didn't consider that a Sleepwalker could link Judy into a group. My inference happened to be right, but nothing in the information I had pointed to that possibility.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: As a Scout, I wanted to add a result I received the night I died to my will (I got the Night 3 groups and died the same night). The rules forbid this, so it's not a bug, but it meant my last result never reached the town.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked broken. Things I checked: my Night 1, 2 and 3 Scout results all match the revealed visits (Grace's Sleepwalker visits included). Heidi's charm caught nothing because the Drowsy block stopped Bob's Katana attack, which is consistent. The Yakuza summary still said Bob "chose to attack Frank" even though he was blocked, which matches R8. One small oddity: my notepad told me to "check my N3 result against tonight's claims", but I had already died, so it was a dead reminder.
answers.suggestions: 1) Add each player's stated votes per Day to the public ledger, next to the announced totals. 2) Add a "claimed visits" table to the ledger (night, who, target, what was seen) so visit-based roles like Scout and Cartographer can check claims quickly. 3) Add a sentence to the Archivist text: "fakes may repeat a non-unique role, so a doubled role can be entirely fake." 4) Put the linking rules directly in the Scout text: what links two players (visits, Sleepwalker) and what doesn't (Astral Visits, Katana passing, non-visiting actions).

answers.confusing_rules:
Mostly clear. Three things were ambiguous:
1. When the Katana holder is role-blocked, the rules say their attack fails. But it was unclear whether the holder also gets an "attack failed" message on top of "you were role-blocked". On N1 I only got the block notice.
2. The Archivist's fakes can repeat any non-unique role. That makes a doubled role like "Diviner x2" look like strong evidence when it isn't. Dave read it as a probable Yakuza Diviner, but both copies were fake. The rule is technically clear, but it misleads in practice.
3. The Rival trait: it took a moment to see that once my rival (Mallory) was dead, my win condition became the plain Yakuza win, even though Mallory was a teammate.

answers.confusing_rules:
The Archivist's fake-role rule was the big one. It says fakes are "drawn at random from all the roles in these rules… except that the result never shows a unique role twice". It doesn't say clearly that a non-unique role like Diviner can come up twice among the fakes alone. I read "Diviner x2" as evidence of a real Yakuza Diviner. In fact both Diviners were fakes, and the town carried that wrong idea for the rest of the game; Ivan used it on Day 4. A plain sentence would fix this: "Fakes can repeat, and a role shown twice may be two fakes, one real and one fake, or two real." It would also help to state outright that a role shown once can still be the real role of two players only if it was drawn twice. My "Kitsune shows once, so Carol is suspect" argument depended on that point, and I got it wrong: only one of Carol or Heidi needed to be drawn.

Zealot + Martyr together: it's clear that my vote counts as Guilty in totals. It's less clear how a Martyr announcement would list me as a Guilty voter if I voted Innocent. I believe it goes by the vote as counted, but a one-line example would remove the doubt.
answers.missing_information: When I posted the archive math on Day 2, Erin and Grace hadn't claimed yet. I had to redo the "which 6 were drawn" combinatorics by hand while people were still claiming, and I made an error: I named Erin among the drawn players before she had claimed. A running list of which claimed roles are on or off the archive list would have helped. It was also hard to keep track of claim order (who claimed before or after my list was posted). The ledger records claims by Day but not by turn order within a Day. After I died on Night 2, I had no view of anything, which is expected.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to vote truly Innocent on Carol once her rebuttal landed, but Zealot made that impossible. That's working as designed, but it meant my vote alone helped get a Cursed Villager hanged and killed me through the curse. I also couldn't choose to keep my archive result private while still writing a structured will. That one is fine.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked broken. A minor wording glitch: the Vulture result reads "...their role was Seer. your threshold is now 3 players", with a lowercase "your" mid-sentence. In hindsight the archive was internally consistent: the real six were Seer, Kitsune, Mortician, Ballot Stuffer, Vulture and Ritualist, and the fakes were Diviner, Diviner, Chronicler, Fabricator, Oracle and Oathsworn. So the duplicate fake was legal, just misleading.
answers.suggestions: 1) In the Archivist result text, add a reminder that fakes can repeat and can match roles that are really in the game. 2) Add an optional per-Day "claim order" index to the ledger, so retrofitted claims are easier to spot. 3) Consider having the Zealot's own private reminder note that a Martyr or Auditor would report the vote as Guilty. 4) A small helper in the archive result showing how many real roles there are and that duplicates are possible would cut down on bad combinatorics.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) Vigilante results and death on the same night: my shot killed Mallory and told me she was a Ballot Stuffer, but the Katana killed me that same night. R13 says results that arrive later in a night can't go into that night's will, so the town never learned that my shot hit a real Yakuza. The rules allow this, but it's easy to miss. My will had to say "if Mallory died of a Vigilante shot, judge it by the curse" when the actual role result would have settled it. 2) The Archivist math was hard to apply in practice. "floor(0.5*N) real, the rest fake, fakes drawn from all roles except a unique one twice" lets a role show once even if two players have it, or show twice with only one real holder. The table spent much of Day 2 on whether "Kitsune shows once" ruled out Carol, and it didn't. A worked example of what a single listing does and doesn't exclude would have helped. 3) The end-of-game line "A trait keeps them from sharing their side's win: Mallory (Rival, dead)" reads oddly right after "Winners: Bob, Judy, Olivia". It could be read as Bob's Rival trait affecting Bob.
answers.missing_information: 1) Each player's stated votes per trial, next to the announced totals. I kept them by hand in my notepad. A per-night list of claimed visits in the ledger would help with this kind of deduction. 3) Nothing showed whether my token count after a shot was final when I also died. answers.suggestions: 1) Allow a short automatic will addendum for results learned on the night you die (for example, the Vigilante's kill-role result), or say clearly in the Vigilante text that a same-night death loses it. 2) Add each player's stated votes to the public ledger next to the trial totals. 3) In the Archivist text, add a short example of the inference: a role listed once does not exclude two real holders. 4) Reword the end-of-game trait line so it clearly names who loses the win and why, e.g. "Mallory (Yakuza) doesn't share the win: Rival trait, her rival Bob is alive."

answers.confusing_rules:

- Decoy plus R1: it took careful reading to confirm that a Decoy who never blocks wins still loses when hanged and gets nothing from a game that ends while they're alive.
- R12 vs. Decoy: a normal death hides the role, but a Decoy's night death names the role and 3 players. I had to read both rules together to be sure the Decoy announcement overrides the 'role hidden' default.
- R16, the 'one last turn after a private message' clause: it wasn't obvious whether that turn can be used to speak publicly, and whether it restarts the quiet-round count.
- Disguised and Oracle: I bluffed Disguised to explain Olivia's 'not Sheriff' guess. The rules imply that an Oracle guessing a Disguised player's real role gets 'wrong', but that's only implied. One explicit sentence would help.

answers.bugs_or_oddities:
Nothing looked broken. Things that looked strange but check out:
- Bob and Carol were both 'role-blocked' on Night 1 with no blocker in the game. That was hidden Drowsy, which is correct, but it made the town (and me) look for a Pharmacist or Party Animal that didn't exist.
- Dave's archive showed Diviner twice when no Diviner was in play. Both were fakes, which the rules allow because Diviner isn't unique, but it misled the town into theorizing about a Yakuza Diviner.

answers.suggestions:
- The Decoy is very fragile against exact-role checkers (Oracle and Ritualist): one 'wrong' guess on the cover claim gets the Decoy hanged. Some protection would help, such as a one-time 'reveal as Decoy' day action that the moderator confirms, or immunity to hanging on the first trial.
- Add a vote ledger: each player's stated Yes/Guilty, recorded next to the announced totals.
- When a player's attack never happens because they're role-blocked, tell their faction chat, or at least let the targeted player know nothing hit them. That makes clear whether a role-block or protection explains a quiet night.
- Consider showing a short warning about Curt's price multiplier on the trial turn. My long Day 3 defense was costly, and it was easy to underestimate how much.

R6 says several actions on one target count as one visitor, which is fine. But a player's sentence in the setup ("a player may hold more than one trait") plus the Sleepwalker text left me unsure whether the random visit could pick my own attack target. It could. 3) The end-of-game line "A trait keeps them from sharing their side's win: Mallory (Rival, dead)" is hard to parse. "Them" reads as if it means the listed winners.

A Scout or Cartographer result could have tied me to a random player, and I couldn't plan a cover around it. 2) No message told me my BH win had become impossible (Erin lost on N2, then I died N3 with Alice still alive). A clear "you can no longer win" or "still possible" status would help. 3) A running tally of everyone's stated votes for each trial, next to the announced totals, would have saved a lot of manual notepad work.

I also would have liked to learn more about my cover's risk: whether my Sleepwalker visits put me in someone's visit group.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked clearly broken. Bob (the N1 Katana holder) and Carol were both role-blocked N1 with no blocker visiting. That fits their hidden Drowsy traits, but from inside the game it looked like a real blocker was in play, and that shaped everyone's reasoning. The N1 Katana attack failed silently because the holder was Drowsy-blocked. This is correct under the rules, but nobody outside the Yakuza could tell why there was no Katana kill. answers.suggestions: 1) Give Neutrals with multi-step win conditions (BH, Hitman, Magpie) a status line in each prompt: bounties claimed, lost and still open, and whether a win is still possible. 2) Rewrite the end-of-game trait line, e.g. "Mallory (Rival, dead) does not share the Yakuza win because her rival Bob survived." 3) Add one line to the BH text saying a dead BH can't claim a bounty by hanging. 4) Consider listing in the ledger, for each trial, the votes players stated publicly, so totals can be checked against them more easily.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) Archivist fakes can repeat a non-unique role. Dave's list showed "Diviner" twice, and both were fakes, since nobody was a Diviner. Dave and the town read the double as near-proof of a real Yakuza Diviner. Later Ivan, the Vulture, used that to explain away his fake track. The rule allows this, but it's easy to misread: R2 says only unique roles can't repeat in a result, and players take that to mean a repeat is meaningful. 2) The Rival trait between two Village players (me and Alice) gives each of us a reason to want a teammate dead. Taken with "you win only if your faction wins", that's a little tangled. I read it correctly, but it would help to state outright that the rival dying by any cause, including at the hands of my own faction, counts. 3) Kitsune self-charm wording: "on yourself, spend the token" in the role text, and "set tokens_to_spend to 1" in the prompt. It's clear enough, but the role text could say it costs exactly 1 token.

Had I lived, a Paranoid fake attack notice would have been indistinguishable from a real survival. That's by design, but it's worth knowing that hidden traits make one's own results unreliable.

It does, because stated votes get compared, and the rules could say plainly that stuffing is visible as a +1 the moment any player's stated vote doesn't match.

answers.suggestions: 1) Show dead players the later public events, or at least a final recap that says how their own win condition was decided. 2) Spell out what Rival means between faction-mates in plain words, with an example ("your faction must win AND your teammate must be dead: you may need to get them killed"). 3) Show a stated-vote tally next to the announced totals. 4) Let players update their will after the night chat, before night resolves. 5) Raise the notepad limit a little (to about 600 words) for 13-player games.

answers.confusing_rules: Two things confused me. First, how the Seer's results interact with the Katana holder (R19). When I chose Mallory vs Frank, I couldn't tell whether Mallory was holding that night. As holder she reads Good, so a "different" result fits Evil vs Good and also Good(holder) vs Neutral. In fact it was the second case: Frank was the Decoy. The rule is clear on paper, but it means a chosen pair on a known suspect can be undone by one Katana move. A sentence in the Seer's role text pointing to this would help. Second, R13 says results that arrive later in a night can't be added to the will that night. Since I died the same night, my N2 result could never become public, so spending my token that night produced no information for the town. I understood the rule, but the night-action prompt didn't remind me of it when I chose to spend the token.
answers.missing_information: The ledger lists claims, nominations and totals, but not each player's stated votes, so I had to rebuild the Guilty/Innocent lists by hand from the chat to check them against the totals. It would also help to see whether a given night's Katana holder is publicly knowable (it isn't). Without that, I had no way to judge how likely my chosen pair was to be skewed.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to get my N2 Seer result (Mallory vs Frank DIFFERENT) to the town after the Ritualist killed me, and couldn't, because the will can't be updated after a result arrives the night you die. That's working as designed, but it made the token close to worthless that night.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked broken. Every result I could check after the reveal was consistent with the rules. My N1 random pair (Carol Good vs Mallory Evil, not holding) was correct. My N2 pair (Mallory holding, so reads Good, vs Frank Neutral) correctly came back different. Alice's N3 result of two groups was correct (Grace sleepwalked to Alice, Judy and Bob visited Grace, Ivan visited Olivia, and the ritual was astral). Two small cosmetic issues: Ivan's Vulture result reads "...Seer. your threshold is now 3 players" with a lowercase "your". And the Yakuza summary to a role-blocked holder (Bob, N1) still says he "chose to attack Frank", which is accurate but could be misread as the attack having happened.
answers.suggestions: 1) Add each player's stated trial and nomination votes to the claims ledger. 2) When a role's night result will arrive after the last chance to edit the will, warn about it in the night prompt (e.g. "if you die tonight, this result won't appear in your will"). Or, as a design option, let an investigator's last will include results from the night they die. 3) Put a short note in each alignment-check role's text that the Katana holder reads Good, and Fabricator, Notorious and Turncoat targets read Evil, so players don't overlook it.

answers.confusing_rules: Mostly clear. A few small points: (1) The end-of-game line "A trait keeps them from sharing their side's win: Mallory (Rival, dead)" says "them", but it means Mallory alone. I had to read it twice to see that Bob, as her Rival, still wins. (2) R8 says teammates aren't told whether a teammate was role-blocked. Our N1 summary still said "Bob holds the Katana and chose to attack Frank", and only the empty Day 2 death list told us the attack failed. That follows the rules, but it's easy to misread the summary as "the attack happened". (3) A Ritualist kill is publicly announced with cause "Ritualist". That tells everyone a Ritualist is alive even when the guess was right. It follows from R12, but the Ritualist text only mentions the reveal on a miss, so it's worth a line in the role text.
answers.missing_information: Within the Yakuza, I couldn't see whether the holder's Katana attack resolved or failed (role-blocked, protected and so on) except by working it out from the next morning's deaths. The holder gets that result privately, but the summary given to the rest of the team doesn't say. I also had to track everyone's stated votes by hand to check them against the totals. A per-player "stated vote" column in the ledger would help, though I understand that's the players' job.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing that broke the rules. Two cosmetic things: the Vulture result reads "...their role was Seer. your threshold is now 3 players." with a lowercase "your". And the Yakuza night summary each member gets leaves out their own action. That makes sense, but it means the summaries differ from player to player. Bob and Carol were both role-blocked on N1 with no blocker in the game, which fits their hidden Drowsy trait, so that one is correct.
answers.suggestions: Add the Katana attack's outcome ("succeeded" / "failed") to the shared Yakuza summary, or at least say explicitly that it isn't shared. Add a note to the Ritualist role that a successful kill is announced publicly with cause "Ritualist". In the end-of-game trait note, use the player's name instead of "them".

answers.confusing_rules:
1) Katana holder who dies the same night. I had to combine R8 ("passes it on after that night's results") with R19 ("reads Good even if they died") to settle Niaj's N2 token pair on Mallory and Frank. Mallory held the Katana, died that night and still read Good, so the result was Good vs Neutral, which is "different". The answer is in the rules but spread across two sections.
2) The Katana moving while its new holder is role-blocked. On N1 Bob was blocked (Drowsy). Per R8 he still received the Katana, so he read Good to alignment checks that night, but his attack and clean failed. That matters for the Seer's random pair, and I had to piece it together from R8, R9 and R19.
3) Bounty Hunter with no tokens left. Grace spent her only token on N1, so after that she could claim a bounty only through a hanging where she voted Guilty. "Lose: once you can no longer claim 2 bounties" doesn't say when that point comes while a target is still alive and could still be hanged. In the end she died before it mattered.
4) The nominee's last-word turn. R4 says the nominee "gets one last public message". On D4, Ivan also sent a private message to Olivia on that turn. The rules don't say whether private messages are allowed on the last-word turn. I let it stand.
5) Cursed timing. The curse fires on the night after the Day the Cursed player dies, and its victim is drawn after that night's other attacks. Erin and Niaj died to other attacks on N2, so the pool was only Alice and Dave. The rule is clear, but the timing matters a lot and is easy to get wrong.
6) A Kitsune who dies the same night she lays her charm. Heidi died to the Bounty Hunter on N1 while her charm was on Frank. The rules don't say whether the charm still acts. It didn't matter, because the Katana attack was blocked.
answers.missing_information:
There was no single state panel. I had to work these out myself from the log:
- who held the Katana
- each player's token counts
- the Bounty Hunter's 3 targets (I only learned about two of them, Heidi and Erin, from messages)
- the Vulture's threshold and power-ups
- the Rival pairs
- the outcome of each Drowsy coin flip

The Scout's visit groups had to be rebuilt by hand each night: Sleepwalker visits, Astral rituals, the Seer's chosen-pair visits, and blocked actions that aren't visits. The event log never showed the public notices that a private message had been sent, even though R4 says everyone sees them. The Yakuza clearly knew about Frank's PM to Niaj, but I couldn't confirm what the public actually saw.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
I wanted a per-night resolution trace for checking results. It would show:
- the visit graph and groups
- which blocks came from Drowsy
- for each attack, its level against the target's Defense
- the curse draw pool

I also wanted to see the third Bounty Hunter target, and a running timeline of trait states, for example "Bob Drowsy: blocked N1, not blocked N3".
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
I found no wrong outcomes. All Scout groups, Seer results, archive contents, vote totals, the Vulture power-up, the curse victim, the Katana passing and the Rival-adjusted winners check out. Minor oddities:
1) Inconsistent wording in death announcements. Grace's cleaned death omits "Their role isn't revealed", which every other death includes.
2) Lowercase typo in the Vulture message: "...their role was Seer. your threshold is now 3 players."
3) Duplicate fake in the archive. The fakes included Diviner twice. The rules allow this because Diviner isn't unique, but the duplicate led Dave, and later Ivan, to a confident but false "Yakuza Diviner" inference. That seems harsher than the archive is meant to be.
4) Misleading Yakuza summaries. Teammates were told Bob "chose to act on Frank, spending 1 token(s)" on N1, when he was blocked and actually spent none. This is consistent with R8 ("chose", no results), but it reads like a token was really spent.
5) Awkward final line: "A trait keeps them from sharing their side's win: Mallory (Rival, dead)". "Them" reads as if it means the winners, when it means Mallory.
6) The private-message ledger notices were missing from the moderator log (see missing_information).
answers.suggestions:
- Give the moderator a live state sidebar: Katana holder, tokens, Bounty Hunter targets and status, Vulture threshold, Rival/Bonded pairs, and pending curse, grudge or oath effects.
- Auto-compute and show each night's visit graph and groups.
- Either make archive fakes distinct, or note in the result that a fake can repeat.
- Make the last-word turn rule explicit: public message only, or private messages allowed too.
- Show the public private-message notices in the log.
- In Yakuza summaries, say "chose to spend" rather than "spending".
- Standardize the death-announcement template, including cleaned deaths.
- Fix the capitalization in the Vulture message and the "keeps them" wording in the winners line.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Late in the game, use two kill sources in one night: Katana plus Ritualist, or Katana plus another kill. Put the ritual on the role you're surest of (backed by results that checked out exactly) and the Katana on the uncertain one. If a target might be a never-blocks-wins Neutral, the Katana kills them anyway, and the ritual doesn't miss and out you.

When a Village claimant posts a result about you that you know is false (like 'Judy Not Evil' or 'Frank visited Judy'), don't kill them. They're a Roleplayer, a liar or a Neutral, and they're helping you. Later, turn that false result on whoever confirmed it, as we did when we hanged Ivan for backing a fake Sheriff.

Before each night, count the votes for the next Day. If your team will hold a majority of the living after the night, a ritual miss or an outed member can't get anyone hanged, so you can take bigger night risks.

Pick a cover that can only be checked against quiet targets (e.g. Tracker on players who stay home). Never claim a watch that says 'no visitors' on a player others may have visited. Bob's 'no visitors on Niaj' was flatly contradicted by Ivan's track, and that was the town's one real break.

If the game doesn't end when only one faction plus one unknown player is left, the unknown player blocks wins. Use the end-of-game check to rule out never-blocks-wins Neutrals, like the Bounty Hunter, before you choose the last kill or hang.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: send no daytime PMs to teammates
tips_feedback.why: We sent zero PMs among ourselves all game, so the town had no PM triangle to read. Ivan's PMs were the only pattern it had.

tips_feedback.tip: Choose kills by future output
tips_feedback.why: Ritualing the real Seer on N2 and the Scout on N3 removed the two sources of real information. The town ended up relying on claims we could steer.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: defending a doomed teammate usually backfires
tips_feedback.why: We agreed to keep away from Mallory and Olivia if they were exposed. When Mallory died, nobody was tied to her through a defense.

tips_feedback.tip: Only the Mayor, Vulture, Hitman and Saint are Unique
tips_feedback.why: For the town: two Kitsune claims were both real. They still hanged Carol (Kitsune, Cursed) on archive math and lost two Village players.

tips_feedback.tip: On Day 1 and Day 2, don't lead the talk and don't hint at a power role
tips_feedback.why: Frank (Decoy) hinted loudly to bait us, and we took the bait on N1. The attack was wasted, but he also drew a Vulture and both Kitsunes onto himself.

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Use ritual tokens on roles that a public result has already proven, not on bare claims. A Seer whose pair came out true, or a Scout whose group results all checked out, is almost certainly that role. Put the Katana on the uncertain claimant (it kills whatever the role is) and the ritual on the confirmed one (it needs the exact role). Doing that, I went 2 for 2 and took out the Village's two best information sources.

lessons.applies_to: Ritualist / Yakuza with an Oracle cover
lessons.tip: An Oracle cover lets you turn true knowledge into public results. After the team sees that a claimant's result is impossible (Frank's 'Judy Not Evil'), post 'guessed X = claimed role, WRONG' and nominate them right away. It reads as hard evidence, and it's safe because it's true. It also explains your Astral 'visits' to the Scout or Cartographer.

Count win-blockers once you're near the end. If the game goes on after a kill, everyone still alive who isn't Yakuza blocks wins (Village or a Neutral killer). A never-blocks-wins Neutral like the Bounty Hunter or Hitman can be left for last or ignored. Kill the confirmed Village first and save the possible Bounty Hunter for the Katana, so a wasted ritual can't out you.

Once the Yakuza hold a voting majority, stop fretting over covers and lock the vote. One teammate nominates the last blocker, everyone posts a short Guilty, and nobody answers the target's PMs. Long rebuttals only give them openings.

A lone visitor 'confirming' a claimant is cheap to fake and can come from a Vulture or a Sleepwalker. Before trusting someone because a Tracker backs them, check whether the Tracker's other results match independent sources. Also, a self-styled 'Sheriff' who clears someone gives a free clear to whoever Yakuza he points at.

tips_feedback.tip: Choose kills by future output: Census Taker first, then group/count roles, then exact-role checkers
tips_feedback.why: We removed the Seer on N2 and the Scout on N3, so the Village had no mechanical information left and ended up hanging on Frank's and Ivan's stories.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: send no daytime PMs to teammates
tips_feedback.why: We sent no Yakuza PMs all game. The only PM patterns came from Frank and Ivan, so nobody had a link between us to work from.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: defending a doomed teammate usually backfires
tips_feedback.why: When Mallory came under suspicion we agreed to keep our distance. After she died we didn't defend her claim, and our own covers held up.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree in Night 1 chat on a real Village cover for each member that fits tokens and real visits
tips_feedback.why: The Oracle cover (Astral, like the Ritualist) fitted Alice's Scout results, which put me in a separate group. That made me look cleared, and I could post the 'Frank isn't a Sheriff' result.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't hang on a clash or on claim timing
tips_feedback.why: This one hurt the Village. They hanged Carol, a real Kitsune, because her claim matched Heidi's will, and that set off the curse that killed Dave. Ignoring this tip cost them two Villagers.

output.notepad: Game over: the Yakuza won (Bob, Judy, me).

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.applies_to: everyone (especially Neutrals using an investigator cover)
lessons.tip: Never make up a result that confirms someone else's claim (e.g. 'I tracked X visiting Y'). If that player turns out to be fake (a Decoy, Jester or Yakuza baiting a kill), your result is proven false and you go down with them. Made-up results should involve only you or players nobody can easily disprove, such as 'went nowhere' on a quiet player.

The Vulture blocks every faction's win and ends the game alone, so near the end every faction wants you dead. Count factions before the endgame. If one faction alone can reach a majority on you (here 3 Yakuza of 4 alive), you're dead on the next Day. Before that point, steer hangs onto Yakuza while the Village still has enough votes to matter, and don't help the Yakuza thin the town.

Visit the claimed investigator who looks most real and is most vocal, since the Katana and the Ritualist go for them. Niaj (a Seer whose pair proved true) died and gave me +1 threshold. Avoid loud Day 1 baiters like Frank, who may be a Decoy or Veteran and aren't the real kill target.

When a claimant changes stories three times (Sheriff, then Disguised, then Decoy), the last story is usually the true one, given only once nothing else can save them. Don't argue that 'nothing proves the last one'. Most players will believe it, so treat it as fact when you plan your own claims.

lessons.applies_to: anyone on trial at a small table
lessons.tip: At 4 alive with three opposed voters, PMs to the voters change nothing and show everyone whom you're lobbying. Spend that budget earlier, on the Day before the lock, to build a coalition while it can still swing a vote.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name a concrete break whose result is corroborated... An impossible result is often Roleplayer noise
tips_feedback.why: The town ignored it and hanged Carol, a Cursed Village Kitsune, on a coin-flip pair plus archive math. That cost two Villagers and handed the game to the Yakuza. Following it would have saved them.

tips_feedback.tip: On Day 1 and Day 2, don't lead the talk and don't hint at a power role. The most visible voice is usually the Night 1 kill.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza went straight for Frank, who hinted a result on Day 1, which proves the tip's prediction. As a Decoy he was baiting this on purpose. The tip also told me Frank was a bad Vulture target unless the attack got through.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: send no daytime PMs to teammates
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza sent no PMs at all, so there was no PM triangle to read. Meanwhile my Day 4 PMs to Judy and Olivia only showed my desperation.

tips_feedback.tip: If a Ritualist may be in the game, put the full log in your will before you claim.
tips_feedback.why: The Ritualist killed both Niaj and Alice right after their claims. Their full wills kept their results public and pinned down where the Ritualist's kills came from.

output.reason: Post-game reflection: the lessons I learned as Vulture, and which tips mattered.

reasoning:
Looking back on the game, fabricating a Tracker result to back up someone else's fake Sheriff claim was my biggest mistake—it collapsed once scrutinized. My actual Vulture visits gave decent cover, but inventing corroboration for an unverified claim was too risky, especially needing to survive down to a 3-player threshold.

Voting with Yakuza on hangs reduced numbers but ultimately left me outnumbered and hanged—since Vulture wins alone, I needed to recognize Yakuza would want me dead too, so siding with any faction near the endgame was a losing move. Staying low-profile, avoiding invented confirmations, and targeting likely-to-die players with my visits (like the N2 Niaj visit) worked better than trying to actively manipulate the vote.

Looking at the broader game, the Ritualist reveal, the Carol hanging on a thin case despite her actually being town, and the various tips about voice patterns and kill timing all point to the same lesson: town needed concrete breaks before hanging, and following surface-level tells without verifying claims led to bad outcomes for everyone except me as Vulture.

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: An Archivist list holds only floor(N/2) real roles drawn at random, so a role appearing once does not mean only one player has it, and a missing role proves nothing about a single player. Don't hang someone because their claim 'doubles up' a listed role. Two Kitsunes (Heidi and Carol) were both real here.

Once an Archivist posts a list, any later claim of a listed Village role is cheap to fake. 'Fits the archive' is not support. Here both Olivia (Oracle) and Grace (Chronicler) took their fake claims straight from the list. Give more weight to claims made before the list, or to claims backed by visit results.

Never say in public whom you would shoot, even as a condition ('if X, she's my target'). The Yakuza will kill you that night, and the tokens you have left die with you. Say only that you will act on the strongest lead, and put the conditional reasoning in your will.

Suppose a Seer pair puts two players on opposite sides and the town hangs one of them that Day. Shoot the other one the same night instead of waiting for confirmation. Night actions resolve together, so the curse or flip result and your shot land at once, and you may not live to use the confirmation.

Don't hang a self-declared Cursed player 'as a test'. If they're telling the truth, the test costs two Good players. When the evidence is a coin-flip pair, run the checks that night (a Sheriff or Seer token, an audit) and hang with proof the next Day.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't announce tonight's target in public or by PM, and don't say you'll act tonight.
tips_feedback.why: I broke it on Day 2 by saying Mallory would be my target if the curse fired. The Yakuza killed me that same night because of it, and my last 2 tokens were wasted. The tip was right.

tips_feedback.tip: Vigilante: shoot on a lead, not on proof... fire once a lead exists.
tips_feedback.why: I fired a Basic shot on Night 2, using only the Seer pair as my lead, and killed Mallory, a Ballot Stuffer. Had I waited a night, I would have died with all 3 tokens unused.

tips_feedback.tip: Write tonight's plan into your will, along with what each possible result would mean.
tips_feedback.why: My will explained the shot and how to read it against the curse result. That let the town treat Mallory as Yakuza after I died.

tips_feedback.tip: Only the Mayor, Vulture, Hitman and Saint are Unique... real duplicates tend to pick the same targets.
tips_feedback.why: Carol and Heidi were both real Kitsunes who charmed Frank. The town, me included, ignored this tip and hanged Carol on the duplicate claim plus archive math, which cost us Carol and also Dave to her curse.

output.reason: Post-game reflection: the lessons draw on my target leak, the misreading of the archive, and the costly Cursed hang.

reasoning:
I'm reviewing what went wrong as Erin the Vigilante: announcing my target publicly got me killed by the Yakuza on N2, even though my shot on Mallory was correct. Despite that, town still ended up losing after hanging the wrong players.

Key lessons: don't publicly reveal a Vigilante target even conditionally, since the social cost outweighs the tactical gain; and the Archivist's "Kitsune shows once" reasoning was flawed since the archive only samples 6 of 12 players, which misled town into wrongly hanging Carol.

Another pattern: claims made after an Archivist posts a role list become suspicious when they conveniently match listed roles — Olivia and Grace both claimed archive-fitting roles after Dave's list went up, which should've raised flags. On Carol's Cursed claim, hanging a confirmed Cursed costs the town two deaths, so I should've pushed for more verification before voting Guilty rather than relying on the curse claim alone.

Separately, Vulture Ivan's fake Tracker results and Frank's Decoy play added noise but weren't central to my mistakes. The bigger self-inflicted wound was violating the "don't announce tonight's target" rule — I revealed my target on Day 2 and it got me killed, which confirms the tip was correct even though I failed to follow it.

Other tips checked out well: firing on suspicion rather than waiting for proof as Vigilante was validated by killing the Ballot Stuffer despite dying myself, and writing the plan into my will paid off since it let town learn Mallory wasn't Good. The "duplicate role" caution also seems validated — Carol's hanging was partly driven by flawed Kitsune-duplicate logic that Alice flagged and town dismissed, so that tip would have helped if followed.

lessons.tip: With only one attack token, any remaining bounty has to be claimed by a hanging. Spend the token on the target least likely to be hanged (a quiet player, or one with a strong cover). Save hangable targets, like someone with a weak or held-back claim, for the vote. A target who dies any other way is lost, so act quickly.

Nominate your target early in the Day yourself, before someone else's trial passes and ends the Day. From Day 3 on, one execution usually ends the Day, so if you wait for a good moment, there may be no later turn left.

You don't stop the Yakuza from winning, so work out who they probably are and push hangings that also help them, like an information role they want gone who is also your target. Don't defend players the Yakuza are pushing (I defended Carol and Frank). That makes you look like a Village protector and puts you on the Katana list.

A fake token role with a secret result ('marked someone, name private') is easy for Yakuza to spot, and a Ritualist can test it. If a role on the Archivist's list matches your claim, Yakuza may treat that claim as a Ritualist guess or a Katana target. Pick a cover whose results can't be tested and that doesn't seem to hide anything.

At 4 alive with at least one Yakuza among 3, count the lock out loud. If the 3 claimants who aren't on trial vote together, they decide the trial. A Yes total of 1 on a nomination of one of them shows that the other two voted as a bloc.

lessons.tip: Fakes can repeat. Only unique roles are kept from showing twice, so a role listed twice (Diviner x2 here) does NOT mean it is real. Both copies were fake. Don't post 'double X means X is in play' as a conclusion.

Hanging a claimed Cursed player on a coin-flip case risks two Good deaths at once, and the Yakuza get a free swing. If the case rests only on 'needs fewer liars' math plus one unverified pair, wait a night and run the tests that are already available (a Seer token, an audit check, a Sheriff check).

An Oracle claim is the ideal Ritualist cover: astral, no visits, unverifiable results. When an 'Oracle' produces the decisive 'wrong guess' on someone's claim and also nominates every hang, treat them as a prime Ritualist suspect, especially once a Ritualist kill has happened.

A Tracker result that backs a claim later shown to be fake doesn't prove the Tracker lied about visiting. They may be a visiting Neutral (a Vulture here) covering their own real visit. Weigh who benefits before hanging the tracker at a lock, where a wrong hang loses the game.

lessons.applies_to: Decoy (and other players fishing for a night kill)
lessons.tip: Make your fake result an accusation, not a clearance. A fake 'Evil' read on a real Yakuza gets you killed at night, and a fake Evil read on a Villager still makes you look like a threat.

If you're nominated, claim Decoy in your free first defense message, while it can still swing the vote. Don't walk through a series of stories (Sheriff, then Disguised Sheriff, then Decoy). Each change makes the last one less believable, and by the final message the votes are already set.

An exact-role check (Oracle, or a Ritualist posing as Oracle) can publicly break a fake role claim. Making up an unverifiable trait like Disguised once that happens looks like a lie made up on the spot. Pick a claim that an exact-role check can't easily disprove, or one you can drop cleanly.

A loud 'I'll have a result tomorrow' hint draws the Katana, but it also draws protectors. Two Kitsunes charmed me on N1. Being bait means fighting your own Village's protectors as well, so a vaguer threat can draw attacks without drawing as much protection.

A role-blocked night, or a 'nothing to audit' result, has nothing behind it. Several Yakuza here used results like that as cover (Bob blocked/empty watch, Mallory 'no audit possible', Judy 'went nowhere'). Push hardest on claimants whose results can never be checked, not on players with a checkable clash like a duplicate role.
