lessons.tip: When an Archivist list includes a Ritualist, treat Oracle claims with extra suspicion. Oracle is the natural cover for a Ritualist: both are Astral, single-guess roles. An Oracle's 'my guess was wrong about X' can't be checked and is an easy way to push a hang. Ask the Oracle claimant for a correct guess that can be verified, and don't hang anyone on an Oracle miss alone.

Match the Evil and Neutral roles on an Archivist list against the claims. Every real role on the list belongs to someone. If Mortician, Ballot Stuffer, Ritualist and Vulture all show up but no claimant fits them, then several 'Tracker/Lookout/Auditor/Oracle' claimants are those roles. Off-list investigator claims that pile up (two Trackers, a Lookout, an Auditor) are the likeliest liars.

Late in the game, count how many real Village players are left, not just how many are alive. Neutrals that never block wins (Decoy, Bounty Hunter) and win-blocking Neutrals (Vulture) take up seats. Hanging a credible never-blocks-wins claimant (e.g. a Decoy whose story explains every earlier lie) throws away a Day. Spend that Day on the players whose story the Neutral's confession exposes, and on whoever pushed the Neutral's hang.

Sleepwalkers and Bounty Hunters add visits nobody claims, so group-based inferences ('X wasn't the Katana holder because X was in a separate group') hold only if every visitor in the group is accounted for. Say how sure you are. Once your results are publicly exact, a Ritualist can guess your role for a certain kill: put the full log and every possible reading of tonight's result in your will before you claim.

Real info roles whose public results are exactly right are the safest Ritualist targets, so spend ritual tokens on them. Put the Katana on the claimant whose role you're less sure of, since the Katana kills whatever the role turns out to be.

tips_feedback.tip: Post any result that bears on a vote in your first speech; results held back look retrofitted.
tips_feedback.why: I held my Scout result on Day 2 until most players had claimed. Grace (the Bounty Hunter) then kept using that delay to point at me. Posting it right away would have taken that line away from her.

tips_feedback.tip: Two claimants of a non-unique role can both be real; don't hang on a clash.
tips_feedback.why: Carol and Heidi really were both Kitsune. I voted Innocent because of this tip, and Carol's curse proved her Village, but the bandwagon hanged her anyway. The tip was right.

tips_feedback.tip: Vigilante: shoot on a lead, not proof.
tips_feedback.why: Erin shot Mallory on Niaj's pair alone and killed the Ballot Stuffer.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: agree on Night 1 covers that fit real visits (Lookout/Tracker/Oracle/Auditor).
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza's Astral-fitting covers (Olivia as Oracle for her Ritualist role, Judy as a Tracker with 'went nowhere' results) held until the end, and the Yakuza won.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza kill priority: Census/group-count roles first, then exact-role checkers.
tips_feedback.why: Olivia's ritual killed me (the Scout) the night after my results proved exact. My Night 3 result, which would have exposed the groups, died with me.

lessons.tip: When you have a Ritualist and the Katana on the same night, aim the ritual at the player whose role is proven by results that were exactly right (a Seer pair that came true, Scout groups that matched), and put the Katana on the player whose claim is still uncertain. The Katana kills whatever their role is, but the ritual only lands if the guess is right.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza faking a Lookout or Tracker
lessons.tip: Don't fake a 'no visitors' watch on a player who died or was a likely target that night. Vultures, Trackers, Seers using a token and Sleepwalkers all visit those players, and one real visitor breaks your claim. Pick a quiet player for a fake empty watch, or claim a visit you know about from night chat.

Once you hold a majority of the living votes, or are one kill away from it, go for two kills in one night (Katana plus ritual or another attack) instead of waiting. A ritual miss that outs your Ritualist can't get them hanged if the town can't reach a majority without your votes.

A claimed Tracker whose result backs up a claim that later collapses (for example, a fake Sheriff who turns out to be a Decoy) probably made the result up. Often that claimant is a Neutral such as a Vulture that visits real targets. Trace the visits that player really could have made instead of treating them as confirmed.

Being role-blocked on Night 1 with no blocker in play can come from the hidden Drowsy trait. Yakuza: if your own team has no blocker and you get blocked, plan for a 50% chance of failing each night. Don't put both the Katana attack and a clean on that one member.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: send no daytime PMs to teammates
tips_feedback.why: We sent no PMs the whole game. The only PMs the town could see were Frank's and Ivan's, so no PM triangle ever pointed at us.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree in Night 1 chat on a real Village cover for each member, one that fits their tokens and real visits
tips_feedback.why: The covers we agreed on (Lookout, Tracker, Oracle, Auditor) matched our real visits, and Astral for Olivia matched her Oracle claim. The covers held up all the way to the end.

tips_feedback.tip: Every member should submit the agreed Katana holder, target and night action
tips_feedback.why: Each night we confirmed the holder and target in chat and every vote passed. Night 3's double kill depended on this.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't flatly deny a visit that a count, group or watch could expose
tips_feedback.why: I broke it with my 'no visitors on Niaj' watch. Ivan, really the Vulture, had visited Niaj and used that to nominate me on Day 4. It only failed because we already had the vote majority, which proves the tip right.

tips_feedback.tip: Choose kills by future output
tips_feedback.why: Ritualing the Seer and then the Scout removed the two sources of information that had proven results. That left the town relying on unverifiable claims.

lessons.applies_to: Village roles that can't be verified (Kitsune, Medic, other protectors)
lessons.tip: If you were role-blocked, give your full claim (role, target, trait) in your first speech, not just 'I was blocked.' Holding back your role until someone presses you looks like you are building a claim to fit, especially when a dead player's will already names the same role and target.

Saying you're Cursed won't keep you off the rope. Town will call the hang a 'free test' because the curse death proves your alignment. Instead, offer concrete checks that can run tonight on the other suspect (a Sheriff check, a Seer token, an audit to compare with stated votes), and ask for one night's delay before they hang you.

Archive math only proves that liars exist among the claimants whose roles are off the list. It doesn't show which claimant is lying, and half the list is fake. If an Archivist's count is being turned on you, rebut it right away: show that every scenario needs at least one liar among the others. Don't let 'fewest extra liars' pass as proof.

When a Seer pair splits a claimant who has some support from someone with an empty, uncheckable claim (an Auditor with 'nothing to audit'), look at the uncheckable one first. This game the uncheckable claimant was a Yakuza, and the town hanged the Villager.

A huge bandwagon (10 of 12 Yes) on a thin case is where the whole Yakuza team hides at no cost. Write down who pushed first and who added small arguments. Once a hang proves wrong, those pushers are the suspects. Here the nominator, Olivia, was Yakuza and nominated every hang.

tips_feedback.tip: Only Mayor, Vulture, Hitman and Saint are Unique, so two claimants of any other role can both be real... Don't hang on a clash.
tips_feedback.why: This was correct: Heidi and I were both real Kitsunes and both charmed Frank. The town ignored it, read my claim as copying Heidi's will, hanged me, and lost a Good player to my curse as well.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: send no daytime PMs to teammates
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza sent no daytime PMs at all. The only PM leads went to Frank and Ivan, so the four real Yakuza never had a PM pattern to answer for.

tips_feedback.tip: Choose kills by future output: ... exact-role checkers ...
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza used Ritualist guesses on the confirmed-looking Seer and on the Scout, and the Katana on the Vigilante. That wiped out the Village's information and won them the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Vigilante: shoot on a lead, not on proof
tips_feedback.why: Erin shot Mallory on the lead from the Seer pair and killed the Ballot Stuffer. Only the Katana killing Erin the same night kept this from swinging the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Post any result that bears on a vote in your first speech
tips_feedback.why: I posted only 'role-blocked' at first and claimed Kitsune only after Bob pressed me. That delay fed the 'copied Heidi's will' story. Following this tip fully would have helped.

lessons.tip: Fakes can repeat. Only unique roles are kept from showing twice, so a role listed twice (Diviner x2 here) does NOT mean it is real. Both copies were fake. Don't post 'double X means X is in play' as a conclusion.

Once an archive or role list is public, liars will pick claims that are on it. A claim on the list made after the list was posted (Chronicler, Oracle) is worth almost nothing. An off-list claim made before the list counts for more. Also note the Evil roles on the list (Mortician, Ballot Stuffer, Ritualist): if the claims add up so that those must be real, look hard at who claims a non-visiting or unverifiable role.

Hanging a claimed Cursed player on a coin-flip case risks two Good deaths at once, and the Yakuza get a free swing. If the case rests only on 'needs fewer liars' math plus one unverified pair, wait a night and run the tests that are already available (a Seer token, an audit check, a Sheriff check).

An Oracle claim is the ideal Ritualist cover: astral, no visits, unverifiable results. When an 'Oracle' produces the decisive 'wrong guess' on someone's claim and also nominates every hang, treat them as a prime Ritualist suspect, especially once a Ritualist kill has happened.

A Tracker result that backs a claim later shown to be fake doesn't prove the Tracker lied about visiting. They may be a visiting Neutral (a Vulture here) covering their own real visit. Weigh who benefits before hanging the tracker at a lock, where a wrong hang loses the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't hang on a clash or on claim timing; test both first
tips_feedback.why: I ignored it. I pushed Carol off an archive clash and her post-list claim timing. She was a real Village Kitsune and Cursed, and the curse killed me. The available tests (Niaj's token, Mallory's audit) would have exposed Mallory the next night.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: send no daytime PMs to teammates
tips_feedback.why: The four Yakuza sent zero PMs all game. Only Frank and Ivan sent PMs, so there were no PM triangles for the town to read.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: choose kills by future output (count/group roles, exact-role checkers)
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza used rituals on players whose results had been publicly confirmed (Niaj = Seer, Alice = Scout) and the Katana on the vigilante and the uncertain claimant. This cleared the board to parity by Day 4.

tips_feedback.tip: Post any result that bears on a vote in your first speech
tips_feedback.why: Alice held her Scout result back and was suspected for it all game by Grace, the Bounty Hunter, and in the Yakuza night chat, which pulled attention away from the real liars.

lessons.tip: An Archivist list holds only floor(N/2) real roles drawn at random, so a role appearing once does not mean only one player has it, and a missing role proves nothing about a single player. Don't hang someone because their claim 'doubles up' a listed role. Two Kitsunes (Heidi and Carol) were both real here.

Once an Archivist posts a list, any later claim of a listed Village role is cheap to fake. 'Fits the archive' is not support. Here both Olivia (Oracle) and Grace (Chronicler) took their fake claims straight from the list. Give more weight to claims made before the list, or to claims backed by visit results.

Never say in public whom you would shoot, even as a condition ('if X, she's my target'). The Yakuza will kill you that night, and the tokens you have left die with you. Say only that you will act on the strongest lead, and put the conditional reasoning in your will.

Suppose a Seer pair puts two players on opposite sides and the town hangs one of them that Day. Shoot the other one the same night instead of waiting for confirmation. Night actions resolve together, so the curse or flip result and your shot land at once, and you may not live to use the confirmation.

Don't hang a self-declared Cursed player 'as a test'. If they're telling the truth, the test costs two Good players. When the evidence is a coin-flip pair, run the checks that night (a Sheriff or Seer token, an audit) and hang with proof the next Day.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't announce tonight's target in public or by PM, and don't say you'll act tonight.
tips_feedback.why: I broke it on Day 2 by saying Mallory would be my target if the curse fired. The Yakuza killed me that same night because of it, and my last 2 tokens were wasted. The tip was right.

tips_feedback.tip: Vigilante: shoot on a lead, not on proof... fire once a lead exists.
tips_feedback.why: I fired a Basic shot on Night 2, using only the Seer pair as my lead, and killed Mallory, a Ballot Stuffer. Had I waited a night, I would have died with all 3 tokens unused.

tips_feedback.tip: Write tonight's plan into your will, along with what each possible result would mean.
tips_feedback.why: My will explained the shot and how to read it against the curse result. That let the town treat Mallory as Yakuza after I died.

tips_feedback.tip: Only the Mayor, Vulture, Hitman and Saint are Unique... real duplicates tend to pick the same targets.
tips_feedback.why: Carol and Heidi were both real Kitsunes who charmed Frank. The town, me included, ignored this tip and hanged Carol on the duplicate claim plus archive math, which cost us Carol and also Dave to her curse.

lessons.applies_to: Decoy (and other players fishing for a night kill)
lessons.tip: Make your fake result an accusation, not a clearance. A fake 'X is Not Evil' tells the Yakuza you're a harmless fake, especially if X is Yakuza, and they'll keep you alive as useful noise. A fake 'Evil' read on a real Yakuza gets you killed at night, and a fake Evil read on a Villager still makes you look like a threat.

If you're nominated, claim Decoy in your free first defense message, while it can still swing the vote. Don't walk through a series of stories (Sheriff, then Disguised Sheriff, then Decoy). Each change makes the last one less believable, and by the final message the votes are already set.

An exact-role check (Oracle, or a Ritualist posing as Oracle) can publicly break a fake role claim. Making up an unverifiable trait like Disguised once that happens looks like a lie made up on the spot. Pick a claim that an exact-role check can't easily disprove, or one you can drop cleanly.

A loud 'I'll have a result tomorrow' hint draws the Katana, but it also draws protectors. Two Kitsunes charmed me on N1. Being bait means fighting your own Village's protectors as well, so a vaguer threat can draw attacks without drawing as much protection.

A role-blocked night, or a 'nothing to audit' result, has nothing behind it. Several Yakuza here used results like that as cover (Bob blocked/empty watch, Mallory 'no audit possible', Judy 'went nowhere'). Push hardest on claimants whose results can never be checked, not on players with a checkable clash like a duplicate role.

tips_feedback.tip: On Day 1 and Day 2, don't lead the talk... The most visible voice is usually the Night 1 kill
tips_feedback.why: I did the reverse on purpose as Decoy, and the Yakuza did pick me as their N1 target for exactly that reason. The attack only failed because the holder was Drowsy-blocked.

tips_feedback.tip: Only the Mayor, Vulture, Hitman and Saint are Unique, so two claimants of any other role can both be real... towns have hanged the real one for 'copying'
tips_feedback.why: It was accurate. Carol was a real second Kitsune and got hanged for 'copying' Heidi's will. Alice cited this tip and was outvoted. Following it would have saved a Villager and the curse victim.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: Choose kills by future output
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza used Ritualist guesses on the confirmed-looking Seer and Scout, and the Katana on the Vigilante. That removed every source of real information, and they won.

tips_feedback.tip: A proven liar may be a Jester / an Evil read fits Chaos Neutrals
tips_feedback.why: Town treated my Sheriff lie as proof I was Yakuza and hanged a never-blocks-wins Neutral at 7 alive. That spent a Day, and the Village lost at parity.

lessons.tip: With only one attack token, any remaining bounty has to be claimed by a hanging. Spend the token on the target least likely to be hanged (a quiet player, or one with a strong cover). Save hangable targets, like someone with a weak or held-back claim, for the vote. A target who dies any other way is lost, so act quickly.

Nominate your target early in the Day yourself, before someone else's trial passes and ends the Day. From Day 3 on, one execution usually ends the Day, so if you wait for a good moment, there may be no later turn left.

You don't stop the Yakuza from winning, so work out who they probably are and push hangings that also help them, like an information role they want gone who is also your target. Don't defend players the Yakuza are pushing (I defended Carol and Frank). That makes you look like a Village protector and puts you on the Katana list.

A fake token role with a secret result ('marked someone, name private') is easy for Yakuza to spot, and a Ritualist can test it. If a role on the Archivist's list matches your claim, Yakuza may treat that claim as a Ritualist guess or a Katana target. Pick a cover whose results can't be tested and that doesn't seem to hide anything.

At 4 alive with at least one Yakuza among 3, count the lock out loud. If the 3 claimants who aren't on trial vote together, they decide the trial. A Yes total of 1 on a nomination of one of them shows that the other two voted as a bloc.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: Choose kills by future output (Census/group/count roles first...)
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza used the Ritualist on the confirmed-looking Seer (N2) and on Scout Alice (N3), and used the Katana on the Vigilante and on me. That removed all of the Village's information and soon gave them parity.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: send no daytime PMs to teammates
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza sent no PMs to each other all game, so the Village had no PM triangle to follow. The only PMs were Frank's bait and Ivan's desperate ones.

tips_feedback.tip: Post any result that bears on a vote in your first speech
tips_feedback.why: Alice held her Scout result back on Day 2, which gave me an easy line to push suspicion onto her (my bounty target). Holding results back made the holder look worse.

tips_feedback.tip: Vigilante: shoot on a lead, not on proof
tips_feedback.why: Erin shot Mallory on Niaj's pair alone and killed a Ballot Stuffer. That was the Village's only Yakuza kill of the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Only the Mayor, Vulture, Hitman and Saint are Unique, so two claimants of any other role can both be real
tips_feedback.why: Ivan and Judy both claimed Tracker, and both were fake (Vulture and Mortician). Nobody tested the duplicate because the tip makes such pairs look harmless, so both fakes went unchallenged until too late.

lessons.applies_to: everyone (Archivist and readers of archive results)
lessons.tip: Archive fakes can repeat any non-unique role, so a duplicate on the list (like 'Diviner x2') proves nothing. Look instead at the Evil or Neutral roles on the list that nobody alive claims (here Mortician, Ritualist, Ballot Stuffer, Vulture). Those are probably the real draws and tell you what the Yakuza can do, so make that the headline rather than the duplicates.

When a random Seer pair says two players differ and one of them claims Cursed, don't hang either on the pair alone. A wrong hang costs two Village players. Spend that night's checks on the pair instead (Seer token, Vigilante shot, Sheriff), and on Day 2 hang someone with a direct break. The pair here was true, but the Village hanged the wrong side of it.

Neutrals with a 'die at night' or Vulture goal will fake investigator claims and results, and those fakes end up 'clearing' Yakuza (Decoy's 'Judy Not Evil', Vulture's fake 'Frank visited Judy' track). Once a claimant is shown to be a liar, throw out every clear they gave or backed. Then re-check the players they cleared first.

The Day 1 player who hints at a big result draws every protector (two Kitsunes and a Vulture all visited Frank N1), and that player may be a Decoy fishing for a kill. Protecting them wastes the charm and adds visitors that muddy Lookout and Scout data. A quieter likely-investigator is often the better charm target.

Count down to parity early. With 3 Yakuza among 7 alive, one wrong hang plus a two-kill night (Katana plus Ritualist) ends the game. Before that point, put the last real hangs on players whose claims were never independently corroborated, like a Lookout with no checkable result and Trackers that only confirm each other.

tips_feedback.tip: Only Mayor, Vulture, Hitman and Saint are Unique, so two claimants of any other role can both be real... Don't hang on a clash or on claim timing.
tips_feedback.why: Carol and I were both real Kitsunes. Alice argued this correctly, but the town hanged Carol on 'Kitsune shows once' and claim timing anyway, losing Carol and Dave (killed by Carol's curse).

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name a concrete break whose result is itself corroborated...
tips_feedback.why: The Day 2 hang rested on unverified archive math plus one random pair, and it hit a Villager. Following this tip would have saved two Village players.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: On Night 1, prefer a quiet but capable target over the Day 1 organizer
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza ignored it and attacked Frank, who was a Decoy fishing for a night kill. The attack only failed because their holder was role-blocked, apparently by his own Drowsy trait. Had it landed, the Decoy wins and the announcement would have named Bob among three players.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: send no daytime PMs to teammates
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza sent no PMs all game and left no PM-triangle evidence. The only PM trails were from Village or Neutral players.

tips_feedback.tip: Vigilante: Shoot on a lead, not on proof
tips_feedback.why: Erin shot Mallory on the Seer-pair lead with a cheap Basic shot and killed the Ballot Stuffer on Night 2.

lessons.applies_to: everyone (especially Neutrals using an investigator cover)
lessons.tip: Never make up a result that confirms someone else's claim (e.g. 'I tracked X visiting Y'). If that player turns out to be fake (a Decoy, Jester or Yakuza baiting a kill), your result is proven false and you go down with them. Made-up results should involve only you or players nobody can easily disprove, such as 'went nowhere' on a quiet player.

The Vulture blocks every faction's win and ends the game alone, so near the end every faction wants you dead. Count factions before the endgame. If one faction alone can reach a majority on you (here 3 Yakuza of 4 alive), you're dead on the next Day. Before that point, steer hangs onto Yakuza while the Village still has enough votes to matter, and don't help the Yakuza thin the town.

Visit the claimed investigator who looks most real and is most vocal, since the Katana and the Ritualist go for them. Niaj (a Seer whose pair proved true) died and gave me +1 threshold. Avoid loud Day 1 baiters like Frank, who may be a Decoy or Veteran and aren't the real kill target.

When a claimant changes stories three times (Sheriff, then Disguised, then Decoy), the last story is usually the true one, given only once nothing else can save them. Don't argue that 'nothing proves the last one'. Most players will believe it, so treat it as fact when you plan your own claims.

lessons.applies_to: anyone on trial at a small table
lessons.tip: At 4 alive with three opposed voters, PMs to the voters change nothing and show everyone whom you're lobbying. Spend that budget earlier, on the Day before the lock, to build a coalition while it can still swing a vote.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name a concrete break whose result is corroborated... An impossible result is often Roleplayer noise
tips_feedback.why: The town ignored it and hanged Carol, a Cursed Village Kitsune, on a coin-flip pair plus archive math. That cost two Villagers and handed the game to the Yakuza. Following it would have saved them.

tips_feedback.tip: On Day 1 and Day 2, don't lead the talk and don't hint at a power role. The most visible voice is usually the Night 1 kill.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza went straight for Frank, who hinted a result on Day 1, which proves the tip's prediction. As a Decoy he was baiting this on purpose. The tip also told me Frank was a bad Vulture target unless the attack got through.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: send no daytime PMs to teammates
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza sent no PMs at all, so there was no PM triangle to read. Meanwhile my Day 4 PMs to Judy and Olivia only showed my desperation.

tips_feedback.tip: If a Ritualist may be in the game, put the full log in your will before you claim.
tips_feedback.why: The Ritualist killed both Niaj and Alice right after their claims. Their full wills kept their results public and pinned down where the Ritualist's kills came from.

lessons.tip: Late in the game, use two kill sources in one night: Katana plus Ritualist, or Katana plus another kill. Put the ritual on the role you're surest of (backed by results that checked out exactly) and the Katana on the uncertain one. If a target might be a never-blocks-wins Neutral, the Katana kills them anyway, and the ritual doesn't miss and out you.

When a Village claimant posts a result about you that you know is false (like 'Judy Not Evil' or 'Frank visited Judy'), don't kill them. They're a Roleplayer, a liar or a Neutral, and they're helping you. Later, turn that false result on whoever confirmed it, as we did when we hanged Ivan for backing a fake Sheriff.

Before each night, count the votes for the next Day. If your team will hold a majority of the living after the night, a ritual miss or an outed member can't get anyone hanged, so you can take bigger night risks.

Pick a cover that can only be checked against quiet targets (e.g. Tracker on players who stay home). Never claim a watch that says 'no visitors' on a player others may have visited. Bob's 'no visitors on Niaj' was flatly contradicted by Ivan's track, and that was the town's one real break.

If the game doesn't end when only one faction plus one unknown player is left, the unknown player blocks wins. Use the end-of-game check to rule out never-blocks-wins Neutrals, like the Bounty Hunter, before you choose the last kill or hang.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: send no daytime PMs to teammates
tips_feedback.why: We sent zero PMs among ourselves all game, so the town had no PM triangle to read. Ivan's PMs were the only pattern it had.

tips_feedback.tip: Choose kills by future output
tips_feedback.why: Ritualing the real Seer on N2 and the Scout on N3 removed the two sources of real information. The town ended up relying on claims we could steer.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: defending a doomed teammate usually backfires
tips_feedback.why: We agreed to keep away from Mallory and Olivia if they were exposed. When Mallory died, nobody was tied to her through a defense.

tips_feedback.tip: Only the Mayor, Vulture, Hitman and Saint are Unique
tips_feedback.why: For the town: two Kitsune claims were both real. They still hanged Carol (Kitsune, Cursed) on archive math and lost two Village players.

tips_feedback.tip: On Day 1 and Day 2, don't lead the talk and don't hint at a power role
tips_feedback.why: Frank (Decoy) hinted loudly to bait us, and we took the bait on N1. The attack was wasted, but he also drew a Vulture and both Kitsunes onto himself.

lessons.tip: Your team winning isn't enough: your rival has to be dead when the game ends, and the game ends the moment only Yakuza are left alive. Start working on it from Night 1 and keep at it, because you may die early. Volunteer the rival as Katana holder on risky nights (possible Veteran, trap or Mirror Maker targets), and plan a late hang of the rival while the team still has a safe majority. Don't save it for the endgame.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza named in a Seer pair
lessons.tip: If a Seer pair links you with a Village claimant who says they're Cursed, don't help hang that player. When the curse fires, it proves they were Village, the pair then marks you as not Good, and a Vigilante will shoot you that night. Push the hang onto someone else and let the pair stay a coin flip.

Pick a cover that already has a checkable Night 1 result, like a Tracker or Lookout reporting a quiet target. An Auditor claim of 'nothing to audit on N1' means you have nothing to show on the Day you come under pressure, and that's what got you shot.

A Day 1 player who loudly promises a result and offers to lead the analysis may be a Decoy, a Jester or bait. If they're backed by one uncorroborated track and their claim changes under pressure (Sheriff, then Disguised, then Decoy), treat both them and whoever backed them as unreliable. Don't spend a scarce hang there when the Yakuza are close to parity.
Your tokens are lost when you die, and you may die early. On a close Day 2 trial that your team wants to go through, spending one token costs very little, and dying with both unused is pure waste.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: send no daytime PMs to teammates
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza sent no PMs all game. The only PM leads were Frank's D1 PM and Ivan's desperate D4 PMs, which pointed suspicion away from us.

tips_feedback.tip: Choose kills by future output
tips_feedback.why: The rituals on Niaj (real Seer) and Alice (real Scout) plus Katana kills on Erin and Grace removed every investigator and shooter, so the Yakuza could hang Ivan 3v1.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree in Night 1 chat on a real Village cover for each member
tips_feedback.why: The Lookout, Tracker and Oracle covers fit our real visits and Astral actions. Bob's 'no visitors on Niaj' and Olivia's astral Oracle claim held up until the end. Only my unverifiable Auditor cover was weak.

tips_feedback.tip: Vigilante: shoot on a lead, not on proof
tips_feedback.why: Erin shot me on Niaj's pair plus my uncheckable claim and killed a Yakuza. It was the right call for the Village, and it cost me the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name a concrete break...
tips_feedback.why: The Village ignored it twice: they hanged Carol (a Cursed Kitsune) on archive math and a coin-flip pair, and Frank (a Decoy who doesn't block wins) on a claim clash. Those hangs handed the Yakuza parity.

lessons.applies_to: Seer (and anyone breaking a two-player 'different alignment' result)
lessons.tip: When a pair comes back DIFFERENT, don't break the tie by asking who claimed later or who 'copied' a will, because duplicate roles are legal. Use outside evidence instead: whose claimed role shows up on an archive or role list, and whose claim can be checked at all. Test the cheaper side first. If one side claims Cursed or something similar and is telling the truth, a wrong hang costs two Villagers, so hang the side with the uncheckable off-list claim before them.

lessons.applies_to: Village power roles when Ritualist may be in the game
lessons.tip: If Ritualist shows up on an archive or role list, a public exact-role claim with tokens left ('Seer, 1 token') is an almost free Standard ritual kill that night. Give your results without naming your exact role, or use your token on the night you claim. Put the full log in your will and ask a protector to cover you.

Spend a chosen pair on a suspect plus someone whose alignment is already fairly settled. Don't pair two unknowns, and don't include a player who may well be Neutral. A Neutral reads as its own alignment, so 'different' against a suspect tells you nothing. Avoid suspects who are likely to be shot or hanged that night anyway.

With an Archivist list, players whose claimed roles aren't on the list are where the liars are, and Yakuza often claim generic investigator roles like Tracker, Lookout or Auditor that won't appear. When archive math says at least one or two off-list claimants are lying, push those claims before the on-list claimant who fits the list.

A track that 'confirms' another player's claim is worth only as much as the tracker. A Neutral, such as a Vulture that visits people, can invent a track to look confirmed. If the confirmed claim later collapses, look hard at whoever backed it, but remember they may be Neutral rather than Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Two claimants of a non-unique role can both be real; don't hang on a clash or claim timing.
tips_feedback.why: I and most of the town ignored it and hanged Carol, a real Kitsune, for 'copying' Heidi's Kitsune will. The Cursed trait then killed Dave as well. Following the tip would have pointed us at Mallory, the Ballot Stuffer.

tips_feedback.tip: Post any result that bears on a vote in your first speech (Village).
tips_feedback.why: I claimed 'Seer, 1 token left' publicly on Day 2 with Ritualist already on the archive list. Olivia ritualed Niaj = Seer that night and killed me. Posting the result was right, but naming my exact role was fatal.

tips_feedback.tip: On Day 1 and Day 2, don't lead the talk; the most visible voice is usually the Night 1 kill.
tips_feedback.why: Frank's Day 1 'I'll lead the analysis' drew the Yakuza N1 Katana attack exactly as the tip predicts. Frank was a Decoy baiting on purpose, which shows how predictable that targeting is.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: choose kills by future output; a shooter, investigators and group-count roles first.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza killed Erin (Vigilante), me (Seer) and Alice (Scout) in order. That stripped the town of information, and they won 3v1.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: send no daytime PMs to teammates.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza sent zero daytime PMs all game, so the PM ledger gave the town nothing on them.

lessons.tip: Use ritual tokens on roles that a public result has already proven, not on bare claims. A Seer whose pair came out true, or a Scout whose group results all checked out, is almost certainly that role. Put the Katana on the uncertain claimant (it kills whatever the role is) and the ritual on the confirmed one (it needs the exact role). Doing that, I went 2 for 2 and took out the Village's two best information sources.

lessons.applies_to: Ritualist / Yakuza with an Oracle cover
lessons.tip: An Oracle cover lets you turn true knowledge into public results. After the team sees that a claimant's result is impossible (Frank's 'Judy Not Evil'), post 'guessed X = claimed role, WRONG' and nominate them right away. It reads as hard evidence, and it's safe because it's true. It also explains your Astral 'visits' to the Scout or Cartographer.

Count win-blockers once you're near the end. If the game goes on after a kill, everyone still alive who isn't Yakuza blocks wins (Village or a Neutral killer). A never-blocks-wins Neutral like the Bounty Hunter or Hitman can be left for last or ignored. Kill the confirmed Village first and save the possible Bounty Hunter for the Katana, so a wasted ritual can't out you.

Once the Yakuza hold a voting majority, stop fretting over covers and lock the vote. One teammate nominates the last blocker, everyone posts a short Guilty, and nobody answers the target's PMs. Long rebuttals only give them openings.

A lone visitor 'confirming' a claimant is cheap to fake and can come from a Vulture or a Sleepwalker. Before trusting someone because a Tracker backs them, check whether the Tracker's other results match independent sources. Also, a self-styled 'Sheriff' who clears someone gives a free clear to whoever Yakuza he points at.

tips_feedback.tip: Choose kills by future output: Census Taker first, then group/count roles, then exact-role checkers
tips_feedback.why: We removed the Seer on N2 and the Scout on N3, so the Village had no mechanical information left and ended up hanging on Frank's and Ivan's stories.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: send no daytime PMs to teammates
tips_feedback.why: We sent no Yakuza PMs all game. The only PM patterns came from Frank and Ivan, so nobody had a link between us to work from.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: defending a doomed teammate usually backfires
tips_feedback.why: When Mallory came under suspicion we agreed to keep our distance. After she died we didn't defend her claim, and our own covers held up.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree in Night 1 chat on a real Village cover for each member that fits tokens and real visits
tips_feedback.why: The Oracle cover (Astral, like the Ritualist) fitted Alice's Scout results, which put me in a separate group. That made me look cleared, and I could post the 'Frank isn't a Sheriff' result.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't hang on a clash or on claim timing
tips_feedback.why: This one hurt the Village. They hanged Carol, a real Kitsune, because her claim matched Heidi's will, and that set off the curse that killed Dave. Ignoring this tip cost them two Villagers.

summary:
The Yakuza (Bob and Judy as Morticians, Mallory as Ballot Stuffer, Olivia as Ritualist) won, mostly because the Village misread its own evidence on Day 2 and the Yakuza used their kills well. On Night 1 the Yakuza went for Frank's Day 1 'I'll have a result' bait. Frank was actually the Decoy. Bob's Drowsy block stopped that attack, which spared the Yakuza a Decoy win and an announcement naming Bob. Grace (Bounty Hunter) killed Heidi.

On Day 2 Frank fake-claimed Sheriff with 'Judy Not Evil', which cleared a real Yakuza. Ivan (Vulture, claiming Tracker) made up a track backing Frank. Dave posted his Archivist list, which really held Seer, Kitsune, Mortician, Ballot Stuffer, Vulture and Ritualist, and argued from it backwards. The town hanged Carol, the Good half of Niaj's Carol/Mallory pair. Her Kitsune claim fit the list and Heidi's will. Mallory's Auditor claim couldn't be checked and wasn't on the list. All four Yakuza blended into the 10-Yes bandwagon. Carol's curse then killed Dave.

Night 2 was a trade. Erin shot Mallory, the Katana killed Erin (she had named Mallory as her target in public), and Olivia correctly guessed Niaj = Seer. Mallory held the Katana that night, so she read Good. That spoiled Niaj's chosen Mallory/Frank pair.

On Day 3, with 7 alive and 3 Yakuza, the Village had its last real chance. Olivia posted a true 'Frank isn't Sheriff' Oracle result and nominated Frank. Frank went from Sheriff to Disguised to Decoy, and the town hanged a Neutral that never blocks wins. On Night 3 the Yakuza put the Katana on Grace, whose role was uncertain, and the ritual on Alice, whose Scout role was nearly certain. Both died, which left 3 Yakuza against Ivan. Ivan's made-up Night 1 track, exposed by Frank's Decoy claim, gave the Yakuza an easy story for the final hang. Mallory's Rival trait (Bob) kept her from sharing the win.

lessons.applies_to: everyone (especially Archivist, Profiler and other partial role-list results)
lessons.tip: Reading a partial role list: roles on the list support the claims that match them. Liars hide among claimants whose roles are not on the list. Before you build a theory, sort the listed roles into Village and Evil. Every Yakuza role on the list (Mortician, Ballot Stuffer, Ritualist, Diviner, ...) is a role some off-list claimant may really hold. Only one copy of a role showing never counts against a second claimant, because only half the players are drawn.
lessons.evidence: Dave's list held Seer, Kitsune, Mortician, Ballot Stuffer, Vulture and Ritualist for real. The off-list claims were Bob/Judy 'Lookout/Tracker' (both Morticians), Mallory 'Auditor' (Ballot Stuffer) and Ivan 'Tracker' (Vulture). Yet Dave's 'Kitsune shows once' argument got Carol, a real Kitsune, hanged. Carol's own rebuttal (liars must be off-list either way) was correct.

lessons.tip: When a Seer pair splits two claimants, hang the one whose claim can't be checked, not the one whose claim is backed by an earlier will or posted results. If one of them claims Cursed (or any trait that costs the town a second player), spend a night on checks first. A wrong hang then costs two Village players.
lessons.evidence: The pair was Carol vs Mallory. Carol's Kitsune claim and her charm on Frank matched Heidi's will. Mallory's Auditor claim had no Night 1 result anyone could check. The town hanged Carol 9-3. The curse then killed Dave, and Mallory turned out to be the Ballot Stuffer.

lessons.tip: If you fake-claim for bait or for survival, don't make up results that name real players, and don't invent results that back up someone else's claim. Fake clears protect Yakuza. A made-up corroborating result ties your credibility to the other liar, and you fall when they confess.
lessons.evidence: Frank (Decoy) faked 'Judy Not Evil' and cleared a Yakuza Mortician. Ivan (Vulture) invented 'Frank visited Judy' to look confirmed. When Frank admitted to being the Decoy on Day 3, Ivan's track was exposed. The Yakuza used that to hang Ivan on Day 4 and win.

lessons.tip: Count down to the lock. On the last Day the Village can still win a hang, use it on your best Yakuza lead, not on a claimant who has a reason to lie but may be a Neutral that never blocks wins. Also look at who nominated earlier wrong hangs: a player who opens every bandwagon is a lead.
lessons.evidence: Day 3 had 7 alive with 3 Yakuza, the town's last real hang. Olivia, who had also nominated Carol, nominated Frank. The town hanged a Decoy who never blocked anyone's win, and the Yakuza killed two on Night 3 to reach 3 against 1. Alice even wrote 'Olivia nominated both hangs' in her will but voted Guilty.

lessons.tip: With an exact-role killer (Ritualist), split the night's kills by certainty. Put the role-guess attack on the target whose role is best confirmed by accurate results, and the Katana on the target whose role is shaky. Moving the Katana to a suspected teammate on a night they are likely to be checked makes them read Good.
lessons.evidence: Night 2: Olivia's ritual 'Niaj = Seer' landed because his true pair proved he was a real Seer. Mallory held the Katana and read Good on Niaj's chosen pair. Night 3: Olivia swapped the plan so the ritual went to Alice = Scout (two accurate results) and the Katana to Grace (claimed Chronicler, really the Bounty Hunter). Both kills landed and locked the game.

lessons.tip: Don't spend the Night 1 kill on the loudest Day 1 player who hints at a result. It is often a Decoy or Jester bait, and a Decoy's death names its attackers. Pick a quiet but capable target instead.
lessons.evidence: All four Yakuza voted to Katana Frank, who was the Decoy fishing for a night kill. Only Bob's random Drowsy block stopped them from giving Frank his win and getting Bob named in the Decoy announcement.

lessons.applies_to: Seer and other investigators with chosen checks
lessons.tip: Pair a suspect with someone whose alignment is already confirmed, not with another unverified claimant. Remember the Katana holder reads Good that night, so a pair result on a suspected Yakuza can be spoiled.
lessons.evidence: Niaj spent his only token on Mallory vs Frank. Mallory held the Katana (read Good) and Frank was a Neutral Decoy, so 'different' looked like it cleared Mallory's side. His will's interpretation was wrong in both branches.

lessons.tip: Don't say in public who you will act on tonight, even as a conditional ('if X happens, Y is my target'). Put the plan in your will instead.
lessons.evidence: On Day 2 Erin said that if Carol's curse fired, Mallory was her target. In night chat Bob cited exactly that to make Erin the Night 2 Katana kill. She took Mallory with her, but the Village lost its Vigilante with 2 tokens left.

tips_feedback.tip: Only the Mayor, Vulture, Hitman and Saint are Unique, so two claimants of any other role can both be real... towns have hanged the real one for 'copying'.
tips_feedback.why: It was exactly right this game. Alice used it to vote Innocent on Carol (two real Kitsunes both charmed Frank). The town ignored it, hanged the real Kitsune for 'copying' Heidi's will, and lost two Village players to the hang and the curse.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name a concrete break whose result is itself corroborated...
tips_feedback.why: Carol was hanged on archive math that Dave himself admitted 'isn't proof', plus one pair that could point either way. Following the tip would have held the hang until Frank's check or Mallory's audit. The Day 2 mis-hang turned the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: send no daytime PMs to teammates...
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza sent no daytime PMs all game, so the town never had a PM pattern to link them. Ivan's last-ditch PMs only went to the Yakuza he was begging.

tips_feedback.tip: Choose kills by future output... On Night 1, prefer a quiet but capable target over the Day 1 organizer.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza ignored it and went for Frank, the Day 1 organizer who hinted at a result and was really the Decoy. Only Bob's Drowsy block kept them from giving the Decoy his win and getting Bob named. On Nights 2 and 3 they followed the future-output logic (Seer, Scout) and it won the game.

tips_feedback.tip: On Day 1 and Day 2, don't lead the talk and don't hint at a power role. The most visible voice is usually the Night 1 kill.
tips_feedback.why: Its prediction held: Frank's Day 1 hint drew the whole Yakuza Night 1 vote. Frank, as Decoy, used the pattern on purpose. A real Village investigator doing that would have died.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't announce tonight's target in public or by PM, and don't say you'll act tonight.
tips_feedback.why: Erin broke it by naming Mallory as her conditional target, and the Yakuza killed her for it that night. The tip was right.

tips_feedback.tip: Post any result that bears on a vote in your first speech. Results held back until after a rival claims look retrofitted.
tips_feedback.why: Alice held back her Scout result on Day 2. Grace and later others used that delay as a case against her, though her results were real. Posting at once would have avoided that.

tips_feedback.tip: Vigilante: Shoot on a lead, not on proof... Dying with unused tokens is the usual failure.
tips_feedback.why: Erin fired her first token on Night 2 at Mallory, using the pair plus an unverifiable claim as her lead. She killed the Ballot Stuffer the same night the Katana killed her, so she didn't die without firing.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree in Night 1 chat on a real Village cover for each member, one that fits their tokens and real visits... keep it.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza set Lookout/Tracker/Auditor/Oracle covers on Night 1 and kept them all game. Olivia's Oracle cover even let her post a true result that got the Decoy hanged.

issues.description: The end-of-game announcement says 'A trait keeps them from sharing their side's win: Mallory (Rival, dead).' Under Rival, whether the holder is alive doesn't matter. Mallory loses because her rival Bob is still alive at the end, not because she is dead. Saying 'dead' points to the wrong reason and could be read as Rival working like Selfish. It should say something like 'Rival: Bob is alive'.

Night 1: the program refused end_phase because the moderator's tell() to Carol was held and not sent. The moderator then re-sent 'You were role-blocked tonight.' The harness caught it and the final notices were correct, but the moderator's first try at Carol's role-block notice was badly formed and needed a retry.
